holidays.name: National French Fry Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crispy, golden, salty potato sticks that make every meal better. Fans celebrate by dunking, drizzling, and piling fries high with cheese, gravy, or just a mountain of ketchup.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as a food holiday on July 13, popularized through restaurant promotions and social media. Its exact founder is unclear, as with many food days.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, fries are claimed by both France and Belgium, and Belgians insist they invented them. American soldiers in Belgium during World War I reportedly called them 'French' because French was the local army language.

holidays.name: Embrace Your Geekiness Day
holidays.description: A day for proudly waving your nerd flag, whether you love comic books, coding, board games, sci-fi, or obscure trivia. No hiding your passion and no apologies.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew from internet and geek culture communities, encouraging people to celebrate their niche interests without embarrassment.
holidays.funFact: The word 'geek' comes from the Low German 'geck,' meaning a fool, and it once described circus sideshow performers before it became a badge of honor.

holidays.name: Gruyère Cheese Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the nutty, creamy Swiss cheese that melts beautifully in fondue and French onion soup. Cheese lovers are encouraged to sample it on its own or in a gooey grilled cheese.
holidays.origin: A cheese-lover's observance that honors Gruyère, a traditional cheese named after the town of Gruyères in Switzerland, where it has been made for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Authentic Gruyère must be aged at least five months, and the cheese's holes are tiny or absent, unlike the big holes in Swiss Emmental.

holidays.name: Fool's Paradise Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day devoted to enjoying blissful ignorance and happy delusion. It invites you to indulge in cheerful optimism, at least until reality knocks on the door.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, humorous observance rooted in the old idiom 'fool's paradise,' which dates back to at least the 15th century and describes a state of illusory happiness.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'fool's paradise' appears in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, where the Nurse uses it to warn against leading a young girl into false happiness.

holidays.name: Rock 'n' Roll Day
holidays.description: A day to crank the amps, air-guitar in the kitchen, and celebrate the music that shook up the world. Playlists, vinyl spins, and impromptu concerts are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: Often tied to July 13, 1985, when the Live Aid benefit concerts took place in London and Philadelphia, drawing an enormous global television audience to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.
holidays.funFact: Live Aid was watched by an estimated 1.9 billion people across about 150 countries, and Phil Collins famously performed at both venues by flying across the Atlantic on the Concorde.
